# Single-crystal references

The separate [fitting references](fitting/README.md) retain one measured-data
FullProf fit per page, with PCR/NEW/OUT artifacts, uncertainties and explicit
model/observation-selection limits. The fixed references below are unchanged.

The source is diffraction-lib commit
`cb2cda7be6117199be8f8cac0a666a7bccd32d90` (`origin/develop` at authoring),
under `docs/docs/verification/fullprof/sc-*`. The local working checkout had
different occupancy and scale values, so every input was read with `git show`.

`generate_fullprof.py` runs FullProf only when authoring these references.
Tests read committed files and never execute this generator or an external
crystallography engine. Reproduce with:

```sh
python tests/fixtures/single_crystal/generate_fullprof.py \
  --upstream /path/to/diffraction-lib \
  --fp2k /path/to/fullprof/fp2k \
  --run-dir /persistent/scratch/fullprof
```

The executable is FullProf 8.40, February 2026. `fullprof.json` records its
path and digest, input/output digests, the raw reflection rows and the
calculated F² table extracted from `.out`. The `.pcr` and `.int` files are
unchanged upstream bytes. `.out`, `.sum` and `.prf` were generated on
2026-10-22. `--reuse-output` re-extracts the existing outputs without running
FullProf again. Output hashes identify these artifacts, not future
reproductions, whose timestamps differ.

FullProf's `.out` gives F²calc to four decimal places, so comparisons must
allow at least half a last printed decimal. The plain `.dat` forms copy
h, k, l, F²meas and s.u. exactly; TOF adds the per-row wavelength from the
seventh `.int` field. Original row order, repeated indices and weak or
negative measured intensities remain data, not an import filter.

These upstream PCRs fix every parameter. Their printed final parameter
sections therefore contain no fitted uncertainties. The pages free only
scale, except the extinction page, which also frees the Becker–Coppens
radius while fitting synthetic FullProf calculated intensities. Its source
explicitly says Becker–Coppens differs from FullProf's extinction model.
FullProf's Ext1 is not a radius or a mosaic spread. No conversion or claim
of parameter equivalence is made here.

The TOF `.out` flags some reflections `Excl`: they are retained in the
reference and marked `excluded_from_fit`. FullProf's reported chi-square
uses that selection, so it is not automatically the all-reflection
objective. No fitted-value or chi-square acceptance tolerance may hide
these model and selection differences.

`generate_projects.py` translates PCR cell, coordinates, B/beta values and
occupancies into `.edi`. Chemical occupancy is PCR occupancy times the
space-group general multiplicity divided by the site's multiplicity,
which FullProf prints in `.out`. No fitted output from crysta is involved.
The slightly above-unity oxygen occupancy in the rounded Tb input is
preserved rather than silently clipped.

`extinction.json` is evaluated with 50-digit Decimal arithmetic. It uses
Becker & Coppens, Acta Cryst. A30 (1974), 129–147,
<https://doi.org/10.1107/S0567739474000337>, spherical nonabsorbing primary
and secondary approximations. The radius/mosaicity conventions and Gaussian
2.12 coefficient follow diffraction-lib's CrySPY backend; the equations
were checked against `cryspy/A_functions_base/extinction.py` upstream at
<https://github.com/ikibalin/cryspy>. The published secondary coefficient
polynomials also appear in the ILL Mag2Pol manual, section 3.3,
<https://www.ill.eu/documents/2169/Mag2Pol_manual.pdf>.

The decimal samples describe one Ni site at (0.13, 0.27, 0.39), occupancy
0.73, Biso 0.41 Å², in an orthorhombic P1 cell (5.1, 6.2, 7.3) Å. Its
bare F² is `(1.03 * 0.73)^2 * exp(-2 * B * s²)` in `(10^-12 cm)^2`;
1.03 is the FullProf/Sears Ni scattering length. Inputs cover both sides
of 2θ = 90°, both distributions, zero radius and zero mosaicity. Radius
is in μm. Stored mosaicity is a dimensionless inverse-width quantity; the
upstream pi/10800 factor is a numerical convention, not a spread-angle unit. Comparisons at distinct scales
check that extinction uses unscaled F². The acceptance tolerance is
2e-11 relative plus 1e-12 absolute for double arithmetic; these are
formula values, not engine regression pins.

The scale-only fitting checks use the closed-form weighted solution on
all measured reflections, including the TOF rows FullProf excludes. They
do not claim to supply the missing FullProf fitted-parameter oracle.

`powder-regression.json` is explicitly a regression pin, generated by
`capture_powder.py` from the recorded pre-feature engine commit. It makes
no independent correctness claim. The same powder input and calculated
array are used by both products to detect changes to the prior path.

`generate_hover.py` derives the selected Tb tooltip witness with 80-digit
Decimal square roots and first-order uncertainty propagation. `hover.json`
uses the separate `report_units/iucr_reference.py` implementation of IUCr
Statistical Descriptors recommendation 12 for the project's default display
rule. It contains no output from the application.

`generate_example_fits.py` authors additional fitted-value references in
`example_fits/`, separate from all fixed parity inputs. The Tb input frees scale,
O1 x and eight independent site-tensor parameters (ten total). Tensor ties follow the four site symmetries. The
Pr input is the installed FullProf Suite's original `Examples/prnio.pcr` and
`prnio.int`, with its twenty fitted variables, occupancies and empirical
extinction model unchanged. Each input is retained before FullProf rewrites
its working PCR. The generator requires normal completion and a convergence
marker; the manifest seals the binary and each input/output file.

Pr's original occupancy normalization is eight times the canonical parity
input, so its scale and scale s.u. are multiplied by 64. Coordinates and beta
tensors retain their conventions; `.sum` tensor values and uncertainties are
printed as beta times 10000. The app gate compares the common scale, coordinate
and tensor quantities within their FullProf s.u. plus half a printed digit.
These runs do not establish an equivalence between FullProf empirical
extinction and Becker-Coppens, nor do they prove that different free-parameter
sets have the same optimum. Those acceptance questions remain explicit in the
hub evidence receipt; no extinction parameter is assigned an invented oracle.
